title: Request Axiom — synthesis sprint notebook
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of customer threads collected during 2027-07 to 2027-08. Goal is to translate raw asks into small experiments (microprobes) that engineering can scope within 1-2 sprints, and to highlight systemic risks that require cross-team attention. This is intentionally rough — notes to self and to the sprint pairing for next week.

Context and signal lens:
- Source mix: support tickets (~40%), partner EAs (~25%), in-product feedback snippets (~20%), sales discovery calls and technical onboarding notes (~15%).
- High-level trend: customers are surfacing two related themes: (A) runtime unpredictability for certain prompt shapes (KV-cache mis-hits + tokenization edge cases), and (B) economics surprise — spikes in token counts driven by retrying, streaming reassembly, and verbose system prompts.
- Severity: several enterprise customers flagged production incidents (brief outages or timeouts) that correlate with large-group batching and long-prefix chat histories. Not widespread but high impact when it occurs.

Representative customer quotes (unedited):
- "We saw a 3x latency tail every morning at 09:00 UTC — same job set — appears to be when many conversations hit the long-history path." — Ops lead, logistics app
- "Embedding costs exploded when we started auto-embedding all user notes; the embed pipeline retried and duplicated rows — we got billed for duplicates." — Data platform manager, edtech
- "Short form answers sometimes splice odd tokens in the middle of the reply. Looks like a tokenization mismatch when we do language normalization upstream." — ML infra engineer, marketplace

Observed patterns and possible root causes (hypotheses):
1) KV-cache invalidation fragmentation: customers with many parallel long-lived conversations are seeing cache fragmentation on dedicated pools; fallback to cold-path kernels shows up as tail latency. Hypothesis: differing session boundary semantics between SDK and server routing cause suboptimal cache hits.
2) Batch reassembly edge cases: when streaming chunks are retried, duplicated tokens get committed into the prompt history; downstream dedupe logic is inconsistent between SDK versions.
3) Embedding dedup/retry loops: idempotency keys not consistently propagated across the internal queueing layer, so retries create duplicate ingestion that looks like higher usage.
4) Tokenizer normalization mismatch: upstream text normalization (NFKC/NFC, control char cleaning) is applied inconsistently and combined with model tokenizer quirks.

Prioritized request list (quick triage):
- P0: "consistent idempotency for embedding ingestion" — enterprise impact, billing spike risk. Ask: ensure queue layer enforces request idempotency within a 10m window and surface a dedupe metric in Console. Rough owner: Diego Ruiz (CS) + Eng-Platform.
- P1: "session boundary contract between SDK and server" — reduce KV-cache fragmentation. Ask: define minimal session-contract in API; implement opt-in sticky-session routing for Dedicated. Owner: Priya Anand + Eng-Serving-Runtime.
- P1: "stream retry dedupe safety" — ensure streaming retries don't modify persisted conversation state; add checksum-based reassembly. Owner: Eng-Console + SDK team.
- P2: "tokenization mismatch diagnostics" — add optional logging flag for customers to submit a short pre-tokenization snapshot with samples (obfuscated). Owner: Eng-Applied-ML + Privacy.

Microprobes (small experiments we can run within 1 sprint):
- Probe A: Add a temporary dedupe layer in embed-ingest that tracks the last 1000 idempotency keys per tenant for 15 min; run on a canary tenant to validate dedupe rate and false-positive profile. Measure cost delta and successful dedupe rate.
- Probe B: Provide a debug build of the SDK that exposes the session id and a session-hint header; route a handful of paid customers through sticky routing to measure KV cache hit rate change.
- Probe C: Create a lightweight streaming-reassembly test harness that simulates out-of-order chunk retries and validates final prompt checksum. Ship to beta customers as an opt-in diagnostic.

Quantified impact estimates (back-of-envelope):
- Embedding dedupe could save 8%–25% of token billing for high-volume customers (based on sample of 6 customers).
- Sticky-session routing expected to reduce cold-path tail events by ~40% for users with >500 active sessions; global impact depends on proportion of such tenants but could cut several P0 incidents/month.

Implementation constraints and risks:
- Sticky sessions increase load imbalance on Dedicated pools — needs autoscale policy tuning to avoid hotspots.
- Dedupe cache for embeddings requires memory and eviction semantics; need to bound per-tenant memory usage to avoid OOM on crowded nodes.
- Shipping tokenization diagnostics must not leak PII; require obfuscation and a privacy review (engage privacy & legal).

Open questions for engineering sync:
- What is the current per-request idempotency surface in the ingest queue? (Eng-Platform)
- Can we add a 'session-hint' header without breaking existing routing or routing policies? (Eng-Serving-Runtime)
- How easy is it to enable per-tenant sticky routing for Dedicated and Dedicated-burst traffic? (Infra + Capacity)
- What observability will we add to measure the dedupe hit rate and the cache fragmentation? Need a metric spec.

Suggested next steps (next 10 days):
1) Triage call with Eng-Platform + Eng-Serving-Runtime + Product-Hosted-API — goal: agree on one microprobe to start. (Owner: Maya)
2) Draft a short implementation spec for Probe A (dedupe layer) and share with Privacy and Billing for early feedback. (Owner: Diego)
3) Create SDK debug build branch and a routing experiment JIRA ticket. (Owner: Liam)
4) Prepare a small customer-facing note explaining the opt-in diagnostics and expected privacy protections; route to legal. (Owner: Priya)

Appendix: short raw logs and traces (redacted snippets) — included here as paste-ready artifacts for eng review:
- trace-20270727-ops-01: tail-latency spikes at 08:58–09:12 UTC; correlated with batch job ids 7541–7563.
- embed-ingest-excerpt: duplicate-ids observed at 2027-07-19T14:22Z for tenant T-114; 72 duplicates in 7 minutes.
- sdk-session-excerpt: client sent session-id null on retry path but added ephemeral-session-1234 on first try.

Notes to self / meeting prep bullets:
- Prioritize dedupe probe first — clears billing pain and has a narrow safety envelope.
- Emphasize low-friction opt-in diagnostics to customers; avoid asking large dumps of text.
- Capture metric targets before any rollout: dedupe rate, false-positive dedupe, tail-latency 95/99, per-tenant memory used by dedupe cache.

Owners and tentative timeline:
- Diego (CS) — customer coordination, sample tenant selection — 1 week to run canary.
- Eng-Platform — dedupe implementation spike — 1 sprint (design+canary).
- Eng-Serving-Runtime — sticky-routing spike — 2 sprints including autoscale tuning.

Status: draft — looking for feedback from Eng-Platform and Product. Will convert to in_review once spec for Probe A is attached and shared with Legal/Privacy.

End of notebook.
